title: Stable twisted equilibria on random geometric tori in every fixed dimension
shortTitle: Random points, stable twist: twisted Kuramoto equilibria on random geometric tori
oneLine: Identical Kuramoto oscillators scattered at random on a flat torus of any dimension have stable twisted equilibria near every integer winding up to a growing limit, proving the Cirelli–Groisman–Huang–Vivas conjecture for every kernel in their class with |z|K(z) bounded.
abstract: Place n identical Kuramoto oscillators at independent uniform points of the flat torus T^d, d ≥ 1, and couple points closer than ε_n with weight K(z/ε_n). If ε_n → 0 and nε_n^(d+2)/log n → ∞, then with high probability, for every integer twist k ∈ Z^d with |k| ≤ c(ε_n+δ_n)^(−1), where δ_n = (log n/(nε_n^(d+2)))^(1/2), there is an asymptotically stable equilibrium whose phase differs from k·x by at most C|k|δ_n at every vertex. The kernel need only be even, supported in the unit ball, positive almost everywhere near the origin and satisfy sup|z|K(z) < ∞; this covers the hard-radius graph, every bounded kernel and |z|^(−α), 0 < α ≤ 1. The result proves the twisted-equilibrium conjecture of Cirelli, Groisman, Huang and Vivas (SIAM J. Appl. Math. 2025) for every kernel in their class with |z|K bounded, and extends it from coordinate twists to all k ∈ Z^d. Further results: at least c(ε_n+δ_n)^(−d) distinct stable constructed states; a basin of fixed size; for bounded radial kernels, a heat-equation limit uniform over all times; and stable weighted harmonic lifts under smooth nonuniform sampling. The key tool is a sup-norm bound for the inverse graph Laplacian, uniform over all conductances above a fixed bounded backbone. AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate; no external peer review, independent reproduction or formal verification is claimed.

keyResults: Stable twisted equilibria (Theorem 2.1, proof): if ε_n → 0 and nε_n^(d+2)/log n → ∞, then with high probability and almost surely eventually, every k ∈ Z^d with |k| ≤ c/(ε_n+δ_n) has an asymptotically stable equilibrium θ = k·X + u with mean-zero correction ‖u‖_∞ ≤ C|k|δ_n, δ_n = (log n/(nε_n^(d+2)))^(1/2).

Kernel class and the conjecture (Theorem 2.1 and Remark 2.2): even kernels supported in the unit ball, positive almost everywhere near 0, with sup|z|K(z) < ∞ (hard radius, bounded kernels, |z|^(−α) for 0 < α ≤ 1); this proves the Cirelli–Groisman–Huang–Vivas conjecture for that part of their class and for all twists k ∈ Z^d, not only coordinate twists.

Many coexisting states (Corollary 2.3, proof): at least c(ε_n+δ_n)^(−d) distinct stable constructed rotation orbits, a lower bound rather than a count of all equilibria; balancing ε and δ gives order (n/log n)^(d/(d+4)).

Basin and long times (Proposition 5.1 and Theorem 5.2, proofs): a basin of fixed size with uniform weighted L² decay; for bounded radial kernels the heat-equation approximation of Cirelli et al. holds uniformly over all times for each fixed smooth winding lift.
Nonuniform sampling (Theorem 6.1, proof): for smooth positive sampling densities ρ and bounded kernels, stable equilibria near weighted harmonic lifts solving div(ρ²M_K∇φ_k) = 0.

Key estimate (Proposition 3.2, proof): a sup-norm bound for the mean-zero inverse graph Laplacian that holds uniformly over all conductance fields dominating a bounded backbone, with no upper bound on the conductances.

narration: Random points, stable twist. An Evidence Press briefing. Fireflies flashing together, pendulum clocks falling into step, generators on a power grid, neurons firing in rhythm: all are examples of synchronisation. The Kuramoto model is the standard mathematical picture of it. Each oscillator has a phase, a position around a circle, and it keeps nudging that phase towards the phases of its neighbours. Now scatter many identical oscillators at random over a flat torus, which you can picture as a square whose opposite edges are glued together, in any number of dimensions. Connect any two that are closer than a small distance. One stable outcome is that everyone agrees. Another is a twisted state: as you walk across the torus, the phase turns steadily round the circle a whole number of times, like a spiral wave frozen in place. On a perfectly regular grid, symmetry makes such patterns exact. With random positions, every oscillator feels a small unbalanced pull, and it was not clear that a stable twisted pattern survives. In 2025 Cirelli, Groisman, Huang and Vivas conjectured that it does. This paper proves their conjecture for every coupling in their class whose strength grows no faster than one over the distance. Once the number of points is large enough compared with the connection distance, then with high probability every twist up to a growing limit has a stable equilibrium close to the perfect pattern, with an explicit bound on how far the random positions bend it. So many different stable patterns coexist at once. The key tool is a new uniform estimate for the graph Laplacian. Couplings that blow up faster remain open, the constants are not explicit, and the numerical examples are only small illustrations. This is an anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed candidate, not peer reviewed or independently reproduced. Published on the fourth of November twenty twenty-six, its paper and evidence are linked from the Evidence Press release page. This briefing uses an AI-generated voice and is not additional scientific evidence.
